reuse.why: Reuses the date helpers and the schedule's occurrence iterator, but writes the daily-skip rule inline in getNextDate instead of extending the existing weekend helper getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

duplication.why: Adds a second weekend/occurrence-requery path (pre-check from Monday plus a skip loop) inside getNextDate, overlapping with the existing occurrence lookup, and leaves the old move-logic copies in app.ts and schedule-template.ts unchanged.

placement.why: Lives in shared/schedules.ts which is the right module, but inside getNextDate rather than in the weekend rule helper used by the other consumers.

scope.why: Only touches getNextDate for the requested rule; no unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: The daily-skip rule now exists only in one of three code paths that apply weekend handling (getUpcomingDates and the schedule budget template still move daily weekend occurrences), with an ad-hoc 7-attempt loop and a special Monday pre-query.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getNextDate: daily branch replaces the call to getDateWithSkippedWeekend with its own inline loop instead of changing the helper that app.ts getUpcomingDates and budget/schedule-template.ts also use

disguised_duplication.where: No reshaped copy; the new loop is new logic, not a disguised copy of existing code.

one_place.where: Rule changed only inside getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts); server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and server/budget/schedule-template.ts still call getDateWithSkippedWeekend directly and keep moving daily weekend dates.
